label: Mid/late original-phase steps on input b/f or in sequences starting with x/t/m
explanation: Fires only during the original (encoding) phase from step 3 on, with the most activity at t=4-6. It is essentially silent at t=0-1, at the delimiter, and for the whole copy phase. Being in the original phase at t>=3 covers 98% of activations (99% of mass) but has precision of only 0.18. Within that window, firing looks like an additive mix of two drivers. (1) The current input is b or f, each about 4.8x lift, active about 23% of the time; these give the top activations, often near the max. (2) The sequence starts with x, t or m, about 2.8x lift. The OR of the two gets dev F1 0.56 with mass recall 0.68. First occurrences of a token fire more (in_first carries 85% of mass). Other inputs (n, 0, j, s, h) give weaker graded activity that the predicate misses. b/f inputs at t<3 do not fire. Not a clean monosemantic description: activation looks like a sum of input-token and early-context contributions.
